285611647_ae8e7717.text: These subicular glutamatergic pyramidal neurons then transmit information to the deep layers (layers V and VI) of entorhinal cortex in a spatially structured manner (MacDougall et al., 2013)(Guinet et al., 2026).

285611647_e5dc070d.text: However, research has revealed high electrophysiological and molecular heterogeneity among subicular pyramidal neurons, with evidence for further spatial subdivisions within the subiculum (Guinet et al., 2026).

285611647_6a173ab1.text: Subicular pyramidal neurons can be classified into three distinct electrophysiological subtypes based on their discharge patterns: regular firing (RF), weak-bursting (WB), and strong-bursting (SB) neurons (Guinet et al., 2026). These three subtypes show differences in their active and passive electrophysiological properties, as well as distinct morphometric features including variations in apical and basal dendritic spread and branching patterns (Guinet et al., 2026).

285611647_7c1687fe.text: Among RF neurons, there exists a divergent morphological subset that bears two apical dendrites, further adding to the structural diversity of subicular glutamatergic populations (Guinet et al., 2026). These subtypes also display specific spatial distributions along both the superficial-deep and proximo-distal axes of the subiculum (Guinet et al., 2026).
